name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district with a well-funded incumbent running for reelection
Schneider has raised $3.0M with $1.7M on hand; no outside spending against him
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
No public polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The D+12 lean, incumbent advantage, and Schneider's large financial edge over an underfunded challenger point to a comfortable Democratic win, and markets agree at roughly 96%. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays near the baseline with a modest trim for typical incumbent overperformance risk.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a surge of outside spending against Schneider would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. He enters the general election with roughly $3 million raised and $1.7 million on hand, while challenger Carl Lambrecht has reported little visible fundraising, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent. Prediction markets give Schneider about a 96% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast leans on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those all point the same direction: a safe Democratic seat with an expected margin of roughly twenty points, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
